title: Replacing conditionals, extracting classes
idea: Replace Conditional with Polymorphism turns each branch of a type check into its own class; Extract Class moves fields that change together into a new class.
points: Smells that call for it: a type-code string, fields only one branch uses.
Each branch becomes a class behind one interface; the caller just delegates.
A sealed interface lists every variant; a new one needs an edit to `permits`.
Extract Class moves a data clump and its rules out together, validation included.

code.title: The problem
code.caption: A type-code `if` chain plus bank fields in one class. A salaried employee gets paid overtime.

walk.text: Fields for every kind of worker live side by side. Most are meaningless for any one employee.
The type check: a `String` kind decides the pay rule. A typo falls through to zero.
Overtime sits after the chain, so it runs for every kind. That is the bug.
Bank formatting is a second job in the same class: the data clump to extract.
Look at the output: Lin is salaried but receives overtime pay on top.

code.title: The fix
code.caption: One record per pay rule behind a sealed interface, and bank details in their own class.

walk.text: The sealed interface lists the permitted variants. A new kind must be added here on purpose.
Salaried pay has no hours at all, so overtime cannot leak into it.
Overtime now lives where it belongs, with a named constant instead of a bare 160.
Extract Class: the IBAN, the bank name and their rules now travel together and validate early.
`Employee` delegates: no type check, no bank logic, just composition.
Building an employee now names the scheme. The wrong field cannot be filled by accident.

pitfalls: Logic after an `if` chain applies to every type; check whether it really should.
Extracting a class but leaving its validation behind; the new class then accepts bad data.
Building a class hierarchy for a two-way boolean; polymorphism should earn its cost.

quiz.q: Lin is salaried: `monthly` 5000, `hourlyRate` 30, `hours` 180. What does this print?
quiz.why: The `SALARIED` branch sets 5000, then the overtime `if` runs for everyone: 20 hours at 45 adds 900.

takeaway: Give each variant its own class, and each data clump its own home.

starters: When is a switch on an enum better than polymorphism?
How do I extract a class without breaking its callers?
Could Strategy replace the sealed interface here?
